passage: Chaitanya, you want to stay up all night before physics? Let your Pradeep Chacha tell you about Class Twelve. I drank strong coffee and sat up with my notes till the birds started. I believed every hour awake was another chapter learnt. In the exam hall my hands shook, and I read a question on lenses three times without understanding it. Formulas I knew by heart had simply gone. I panicked and wrote half answers. Before the next paper, my friend Latha sat me down, and she made me a plan: hard chapters in the afternoon, a light look in the evening, and bed at the usual time. I walked in calm and remembered far more. The sleep was part of the studying.

qa.q: Which question did Pradeep read three times?
What was Pradeep feeling in the exam hall?
qa.a: He felt panicked and shaken; his hands shook and formulas he knew by heart had gone.

qa.q: What was the turning point before the next paper, and why did it help?
qa.a: Following Latha's plan to study the hard chapters earlier and go to bed at the usual time; rested, he walked in calm and remembered more.

qa.q: How might Latha have seen Pradeep's all-night habit?
qa.a: Latha probably saw it was hurting more than helping, which is why the plan kept his sleep.

grounding: Shows a student who crams all night believing more hours awake mean more learning, then panics and forgets, and a calmer plan that protects sleep.

passage: The night before the chemistry exam, a wedding band thundered two lanes away, and Varun gave up on sleep. "I'll just go through everything once more," he told himself, and when the power went too, he kept cramming by torchlight. By dawn the equations swam. On the way to the bus he couldn't recall the first flashcard, and his chest felt tight. His sister Indu stopped walking. "Breathe with me. In. Out. You've studied for weeks. You're not starting from zero." He breathed slowly and wrote what he could. That evening Indu helped him plan for the next paper: finish revising by dinner, then earplugs and lights out.

qa.q: What was thundering the night before the chemistry exam?
qa.a: A wedding band, two lanes away.

qa.q: What was Varun feeling on the way to the bus?
qa.a: He felt panicky; his chest was tight and he could not recall the first flashcard.

qa.q: What is wiser about the plan for the next paper?
qa.a: Finishing revision by dinner and then sleeping means he goes in rested instead of foggy and panicked.

qa.q: How does Indu see Varun's panic?
qa.a: She sees him as prepared but exhausted, so she calms his breathing and reminds him he has studied for weeks.

grounding: Illustrates a student cramming through the night, facing foggy memory and rising panic the next day, then planning to protect sleep before the next exam.
